record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transform method be used to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line with Robin boundary conditions at x=0, while controlling the singularities introduced by the extension to x<0?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open problem to use the Bikbaev–Tarasov method to solve the IBVP for defocusing NLS, iut = uxx − 2|u|2u, with Robin boundary conditions at x = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
  i u_t = u_{xx} - 2|u|^2 u,   x > 0, t > 0,
posed on the half-line, with initial data u(x,0) = u_0(x), x ≥ 0, and homogeneous Robin boundary condition at the origin,
  u_x(0,t) + α u(0,t) = 0,   t > 0,   α ∈ ℝ.

The Bikbaev–Tarasov method consists of using a Bäcklund (auto-)transformation of NLS, compatible with the Robin boundary condition, to extend the half-line solution u(x,t) to a function ũ(x,t) defined for all x ∈ ℝ that solves the defocusing NLS equation on the full line; one then attempts to apply the inverse scattering transform / Riemann–Hilbert machinery to ũ. A central difficulty is that the Bäcklund extension may introduce singularities in ũ for x < 0 that must be controlled.

Problem. Develop the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-extension approach for the defocusing NLS with Robin boundary conditions on the half-line: produce a well-defined extension ũ(x,t) of u(x,t) to all x ∈ ℝ which solves defocusing NLS, give a rigorous control of the singularities of ũ on x < 0 (e.g. their location, finiteness, and integrability properties), and use this construction to solve the initial–boundary value problem above, including a description of the solution and its long-time asymptotics for general α ∈ ℝ and suitable classes of initial data u_0.
artifact.status_search_result: The defocusing NLS half-line problem with Robin boundary conditions has been studied by Its, Lee, and Sulem (Proc. London Math. Soc., 2023), who established long-time asymptotics and stability of stationary solitons. However, their approach uses the Fokas unified transform method together with Deift–Zhou steepest descent, not the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-extension method. The specific question of whether the Bikbaev–Tarasov method can be adapted (with controlled singularities on x<0) to solve this defocusing IBVP appears not to have been addressed in the literature found, and is plausibly still open.

status_evidence.title: The nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the half-line with homogeneous Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Approach based on the unified transform method (UTM) of Fokas and nonlinear steepest descent; treats defocusing and focusing cases on the half-line with Robin BC.
status_evidence.claim: Defocusing NLS half-line Robin IBVP has been analyzed, but via Fokas UTM rather than the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund method named in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Absorption/emission of one soliton by a boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Bäcklund transformation used to extend half-line solution to whole line; framework related to Bikbaev–Tarasov approach for NLS with Robin BC.
status_evidence.claim: Bäcklund-extension techniques for NLS on the half-line are actively studied, but a complete defocusing treatment controlling singularities is not established.
